finland.title: Flag of Finland

colors.note: Called 'sea blue'; represents Finland's lakes and northern sky

desc:
- A blue Nordic cross on a white field, adopted shortly after Finnish independence
- The colours reflect the contrast between blue lakes and white winter landscapes
- Official colour standards were defined in 1995 in CIE 1931 and CIE 1976 systems
- **Construction:** a blue Nordic cross on a white field
- The cross is offset toward the hoist
- The vertical arm divides the flag in the ratio 5:3 horizontally
- The cross arm width is 3/11 of the flag's height
- Official ratio 11:18
trivia:
- The cross follows the Nordic tradition but the shade of blue has no official Pantone — it's defined by law as 'sea blue'
- The blue represents the thousands of lakes and seas of Finland
- Adopted in 1918 upon independence from Russia; Finland was the last Nordic nation to adopt a national flag
